Subject: Acme - Invoice estimate & cost model follow-up

Hi Emily / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation and helpful context on your expected patterns. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the key inputs we used for the attached cost model and the next steps so you have a single place to review: 

Key inputs we modeled (see attached ACME_Redwood_Cost_Model_v2.xlsx and pricing_calculator CSV):
- Typical prompt+response median length: ~450 tokens/request
- Estimated peak QPS: 8 requests/sec (spiky burst to 20 for short windows)
- Working averages: 30M tokens/day (~900M tokens/month) for initial pilot; scale scenario up to 1.8B tokens/month
- Target unit economics: you mentioned wanting to be around $7–$10 per 1M tokens for production scale — we modeled a $8 target in the base case

High-level invoice estimate (monthly) — base case (900M tokens/month):
- Model compute (redwood-1-standard): $8.50 per 1M tokens -> $7,650/month
- Platform & infra (caching, routing, SLA): $1.10 per 1M tokens -> $990/month
- Support & observability add-on: flat $1,200/month
- Estimated total (monthly): ~$9,840 -> ~$10.9 per 1M tokens (note: this is before any volume discount)

What we recommend next:
1) Review the attached workbook (tabbed: "base_case", "scale_case", "discount_scenarios"). The CSV is a simplified pricing calculator you can open in Sheets.
2) Call with Aditya (SE) and your SRE on Wed/Thu to walk traffic patterns and caching opportunities — that often drops effective cost by 15–30% for chat-heavy workloads.
3) If the numbers look reasonable, Marissa can produce a formal invoice estimate and draft PO terms (we can apply tiered discounts starting at 500M and 1.5B).

Couple of quick notes on assumptions:
- We model a conservative 12% hit from uncacheable generation (creative completions).
- Quantized model variants (dedicated) can reduce model compute to ~$3.50 per 1M tokens but require a Dedicated commitment and slightly higher latency.

Attachments: ACME_Redwood_Cost_Model_v2.xlsx (detailed calc), acme_pricing_calculator_20260322.csv (simple inputs).

Open to feedback — I can update the workbook if you want to change the tokens/request or target $/1M.

Best,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

2) For the quantized/dedicated option ($3.50 per 1M listed), can you confirm typical latency increase (p50/p95) and whether auto-failover to hosted is supported for peak bursts?

Subject: Re: Acme - Invoice estimate & cost model follow-up

Emily — quick answers inline then a suggested next step: 

1) Blended $8 in the base case was modeled without an applied enterprise discount — it's the outcome of hosted list compute + infra. For volume tiers:
   - 0–500M/mo: base pricing as modeled (no extra discount)
   - 500M–1.5B/mo: standard tiered discount -> effective reduce of ~20% on compute lines (brings blended toward ~$6.5–$7.0 per 1M)
   - >1.5B/mo: custom pricing (we typically target ~30–45% reduction with a committed plan and Dedicated options)

   Example: at ~1B/month our model shows effective blended ~ $6.9 per 1M after the 20% compute discount (monthly total ~ $6,900 compute + $1,100 infra + $1,200 support = ~$9,200 -> ~9.2 per 1M).

2) Quantized / Dedicated tradeoffs:
   - Typical p50/p95 change vs hosted-standard: p50 + ~25–35ms, p95 + ~80–150ms depending on batch/sequence length. For many chat apps that's acceptable; for strict low-latency endpoints we recommend dedicated lighter quantized variants and pinned capacity.
   - Auto-failover: yes — we support policy-based fallback to hosted variants for burst capacity; however that requires cross-model compatibility and a small extra routing fee (we model that as ~$0.20 per 1M when exercised).

Next step: Aditya — can you run a quick "what-if" in tab "discount_scenarios" for a 1B/month steady state and also for a 3B/month burst pattern (50% of month at base, 50% at burst) and attach an updated PDF invoice estimate? Marissa — once we have that I can send a formal three-option invoice (hosted standard, hosted with tiered discount, and dedicated commit) for Emily's finance review.

Thanks — Sean
